newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Loyola says Oct trade gap not a concern.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Loyola says Oct trade gap not a concern.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank chief Gustavo Loyola said October's trade deficit, forecast by analysts at $900 million, is not worrisome and the bank plans no change in its foreign exchange policy to deal with the swelling gap.
"It (October's projected trade deficit) is not a concern. It's normal," Loyola told reporters before a seminar on Brazil's financial system.

He said that the Central Bank will continue its policy of gradually reducing interest rates and denied that the government would seek to depreciate the real currency to reduce the country's trade deficit.

Speculation has risen after Brazil posted a surprising $655 million trade gap in September. Analysts project October's trade gap between $900 million and $1.0 billion due to seasonal factors and strong imports of capital goods and petroleum.

Earlier today, the Central Bank set an extraordinary auction of Treasury Notes (NTNs) for Monday, a move seen by analysts as a bid to calm fears the government would seek to speed the real's depreciation to shrink the trade gap.
Market traders expect Brazil's October trade data to be announced later this week.
